mirror_defect.statement: Not a defect to fix at the mirror. The mirror refuses .parquet by design: COERCED_SUFFIXES at lambda_function.py:77 and the _is_raw gate at :493 (ruling 16, header lines 19-30: a parquet is schema-coerced and its raw content is not recoverable), so widening the rule would launder coerced files into bronze. The seven positions days (2026-07-01, 2026-07-03, 2026-07-04, 2026-07-05, 2026-08-06, 2026-09-28, 2026-09-29) have no flat key to copy, so the mirror is not where they are lost. The one mirror-side gap is that coerced skips are counted per cycle at line 494 without naming the day; that is a denominator observation for the CTO, not a re-pull requirement.

positions.pacing: Code: AdaptiveRateLimiter (data/inf/scripts/bronze/rate_limiter.py) with safe_floor 2.0 req/s (line 112), +0.5 per clean batch up to an observed ceiling, -1.0 on 401/429/503/504, and throttle() sleeps 1/rate before each request (line 251-254); DEFAULT_RETRIES 3. The docstring's 0.5 req/s floor is stale (surprise row IRPT_BCKEND-D2-W396-S5).
positions.days_basis: 7 parquet-only days, including 3 non-trading days the calendar-grain feed keeps. Requests = 320 households x 7 days, one per-client assets request per household per date, retries excluded.
positions.notes: Households: 320 distinct household_id values in the newest silver/api_dims/household_rep_mapping partition (snapshot_date 2026-10-14, 320 rows), counted in scratch, no id recorded. Hours = 2240 / 2.0 req/s / 3600 = 0.311 h at the floor rate; a learned rate above the floor shortens it, and the persisted rate state was not read. Upper bound on time, lower bound on requests.

transactions.pacing: Same shared limiter (rate_limiter.py: floor 2.0 req/s, throttle before each request at data/inf/manual_api/pull_inflection_transactions_rest.py:229); DAILY_WINDOW_DAYS 7 at line 93 sets the incremental window per account.
transactions.days_basis: 0 silently dropped days, so 0 requests for the dropped-day definition.
transactions.notes: Seven trading days have no transactions object in either format (2026-07-01, 2026-07-13, 2026-07-14, 2026-07-15, 2026-08-06, 2026-09-28, 2026-09-29). Upper bound: 863 accounts (distinct account_id in the newest silver/api_dims/accounts_v2 partition, counted in scratch) x 7 dates = 6041 account-level requests, one per account per date; a 7-day window can cover several dates in one run, so the true count can be lower. Hours = 6041 / 2.0 / 3600 = 0.839. Transactions and performance are not counted from the Lambda handler (inf-api-txn), which has no throttle call in the read.

performance.pacing: Same shared limiter (floor 2.0 req/s; throttle before each request at data/inf/manual_api/pull_inflection_performance_rest.py:222; _fetch_window at line 207; DEFAULT_RETRIES 3).
performance.days_basis: 0 silently dropped days, so 0 requests for the dropped-day definition.
performance.notes: Twenty-two trading days have no performance object in either format. Lower bound: 320 households x 22 dates = 7040 requests at one window per household per date; the sub-year windows of the full-history path would add requests. Hours = 7040 / 2.0 / 3600 = 0.978.

fold_design.schedule: One EventBridge Scheduler schedule, cron(0 6 * * ? *) with timezone America/New_York (10:00 UTC in EDT, 11:00 UTC in EST), fires the Orion raw producer for the three Inflection feeds: the bronze-runner path (inf-bronze-trigger starts the inf-bronze-runner EC2, which runs orchestrator.py) extended with a positions dim, and the flat writers in data/inf/manual_api. It moves the three feeds off the 11:15-11:32 UTC rules (opal-inf-bronze-runner-cron, inf-api-positions-daily, inf-api-txn-daily) in one S2 release, never alongside them. The input JWT rule opal-inf-jwt-fetch fires at 09:50 UTC, before the 06:00 New York fire in both offsets. The other live rules (accounts, reps, assets, eclipse) are listed for the S2 release and not decided here.
fold_design.builder_names: Every schedule, rule and function name comes from lib/opal_naming.py name() output (CLAUDE.md rule 30): name(system, scope, function, kind) with a SCHEDULE cadence as the kind, and the same call for the function. No name is typed by hand. A grep of infra/logic/registry/event_rules.json finds the silver-chain rule and no raw-producer schedule, so the first builder call for this producer is expected to refuse; the refusal is a registry row to add, not a workaround.
fold_design.trading_day_frontier: The producer stamps the frontier with lib/trading_calendar.py expected_last_trading_day(now): today on a trading day, else the prior trading day. The pull date is the feed's calendar day (prev_trading_day(now) for the trading-day stamp), because the positions feed keeps every calendar day. On a non-trading day the 06:00 fire still runs: it pulls the calendar day it owes and stamps the frontier at the last trading day, and freshness is read as trading_days_behind against that stamp, never against a calendar day.

i2_feed.statement: Not yet written. The round-116 B-IN read (checks/r116/p116_orion.py, record ORION_ACCOUNT_PERFORMANCE_READ_R116.json under 0.9.0_WK_IRPT_DASHBD~304) asks whether Orion exposes an account-level performance or return series; that record is not in this tree. If it does, that series is the one feed ~I2 may add, and the round-115 drain end says fact_performance carries only client, date and factor, so the account grain is a source the three feeds here do not hold.

notes: What each fact rests on: the raw-producer site is the repo line read at base b0ec635168; the census counts are LIST output over the two buckets read 2026-10-15 with the day rule in denominator_note; the trading-day flags and the source-absent counts come from lib/trading_calendar.py trading_days_between and is_trading_day (a local computation, no vendor call).

Raw producer: the flat positions writer is data/inf/manual_api/pull_inflection_positions_daily.py:445; the flat transactions and performance writers are pull_inflection_transactions_rest.py:585 and pull_inflection_performance_rest.py:639. Surprise row IRPT_BCKEND-D2-W396-S1 refines the premise of IRPT_BCKEND-D2-W394-S3.

Live writer not located: no scheduled rule fires at 11:51 UTC, the bronze-runner orchestrator has no positions dim, object metadata is empty; the daily flat key's writer is recorded as surprise row IRPT_BCKEND-D2-W396-S2 and was not identified.
Batch history: 2259 flat positions objects share LastModified 2026-07-01 (surprise row IRPT_BCKEND-D2-W396-S7); the per-day writer for the daily keys after 2026-07-10 is the same open question as S2.

The mirror's stop account does not reach 2026-09-28 and 2026-09-29, which fall after the 2026-08-14 restart (surprise row IRPT_BCKEND-D2-W396-S3). The mirror's header count of ten parquet-only dates was not re-derived; this read finds seven for positions and none for the other two feeds.

Source-absent days: transactions 7 and performance 22 trading days have no object in either format (surprise row IRPT_BCKEND-D2-W396-S4). The census definition reads them as zero dropped days; the cost block carries their request counts separately.

Pacing: the code floor is 2.0 req/s while the docstring says 0.5 (surprise row IRPT_BCKEND-D2-W396-S5). The stale clock text of the bronze-runner rule and trigger header is surprise row IRPT_BCKEND-D2-W396-S6.

Counts: 320 households (newest household_rep_mapping partition) and 863 accounts (newest accounts_v2 partition) were counted from a GET to scratch, which was removed; no id was recorded. The request counts are arithmetic from those counts and the day lists, not vendor measurements, so every cost claim is inferred.

Not read: the body of any bronze or silver object; the JWT object and every secret value; the persisted rate-limiter state in S3; the Lambda transactions handler's request loop beyond the throttle grep; the performance full-history window path; the accounts, reps, assets and eclipse rules beyond the S2 list; the log groups (14-day retention); the I2 round-116 record, which is absent from this tree.
rows_written counts warehouse data rows and is 0. The seven surprise rows IRPT_BCKEND-D2-W396-S1 to S7 are appended to the investigation channel and are not data rows.
No Orion API request was made, no Lambda was invoked, no AWS write, sign-in or secret read was made; the AWS calls were list, head, describe, get and filter reads under the worker identity.
The order file and the check were not edited, and its status was not flipped.
